extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO disciplinary staff, and counsel involved in reciprocal discipline proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedure and standards for imposing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 (and statutory authority 35 U.S.C. § 32), including notice/service requirements, opportunity to respond, grounds for opposition, and publication/notification obligations when a state disciplinary authority has reprimanded a patent practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to impose reciprocal discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Action taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 to impose discipline identical to that imposed by a state disciplinary authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may order reciprocal discipline when a practitioner has been disciplined by a duly constituted authority of a State in relation to their representation in a patent matter. (Page references: 'This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for opposing reciprocal discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent may file a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline within the time allowed, based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order provided Respondent opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing reciprocal discipline based on the enumerated regulatory reasons. The specific reasons are set forth in the cited regulation; failure to raise them timely forecloses dispute on those grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office must mail the Notice and Order by certified mail to the respondent at the most recent address provided to the OED Director pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.1l(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order was mailed by certified mail (receipt no. provided) and delivered to Respondent on a specific date. Proper mailing to the address on file and proof of delivery are integral to establishing that the respondent received notice and the opportunity to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response timeframe and consequence of non-response
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is given forty (40) days to file a response; if no response is filed, there is deemed to be no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In light of failure to file a response, the order determined there was no genuine issue of material fact under § 11.24(d) and that reprimand was the appropriate discipline. Absence of timely response supports imposition of reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for imposing discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discipline under the USPTO rules may be predicated upon a practitioner's receipt of discipline by a state authority concerning representation in a patent matter, constituting a violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice of Public Reprimand states Mr. McLaughlin 'be reprimanded for violating 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), predicated upon receiving a reprimand on ethical grounds by a duly constituted authority of a State in relation to his representation of a client in a patent matter.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of state findings, stipulations, and affidavits as supporting evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: State disciplinary findings, affidavits, and stipulations acknowledging sufficient evidence may be used to establish the factual basis for USPTO reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order notes Respondent executed an affidavit acknowledging sufficient evidence to prove by clear and convincing evidence the material facts constituting a violation of the Connecticut Rules (Rule 1.3), and that pursuant to his stipulation the state committee issued a reprimand. Such state admissions and stipulations support reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and publication of the public reprimand notice
rubrics_metrics.description: When imposing public discipline, the OED Director must publish a Notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the specified text describing the practitioner, the violation, and the basis for discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order directs publication of a Notice of Public Reprimand and provides the exact sample text to be made materially consistent with the Official Gazette publication, including practitioner name, registration number, the rule violated, summary of the state proceeding, and a FOIA reading room link for disciplinary decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification obligations to state agencies, courts, and the public (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice of the public discipline and reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where the respondent is admitted, to courts where the respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order specifically requires giving notice pursuant to § 11.59 to state disciplinary agencies, courts where admitted, and the public; this is a discrete post-discipline notification obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of disciplinary decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions are made available for public review at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's FOIA Reading Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice directs readers to 'Disciplinary decisions are available for public review at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's FOIA Reading Room' and provides the URL. This establishes transparency and public access as part of the discipline process.
